text: Cover shall propose, for each shift left empty by a sick call, who to ask and in what order, under a written call-in rule the clinic has adopted, and shall never propose a cover that breaks the rota policy.
acceptance: All children verified.
rationale: POLICY.md governs the planned rota. Nothing governs the morning phone call, so whoever answers it decides, and the habit becomes the rule.

text: The call-in rule shall exist as a clause the clinic can read, amend and sign, separate from the code.
acceptance: All children verified.
rationale: A rule that lives only in code is decided by whoever wrote the code.

text: The draft clause shall state the order of asking, the tie-break, what counts toward a person's turn (covers, asks, or both), when the counts reset, and what happens when no lawful cover remains.
acceptance: I-RULE-DOC: a reviewer who did not write the clause finds each of the five items stated, and finds that every parameter the controller reads is named in the clause.
rationale: Each of the five is a choice someone will otherwise make silently.

text: The controller shall carry no count from one rota period into the next unless the adopted clause grants it.
acceptance: T-RULE-RESET passes: with the reset clause set, the call order on day 1 of a period is identical whatever happened in the previous period, over 1000 seeded histories.
rationale: A cross-period tally would make the program the clinic's memory of who owes whom, a power the policy never gave it (rota sessions 3-4).

text: The des model shall reproduce the planned rota, sick calls and the morning phone well enough to compare call-in rules.
acceptance: All children verified.
rationale: Rules are compared before anyone is asked to live under one.

text: With the sickness rate set to zero, the model shall make no calls and every planned shift shall be worked by the planned person.
acceptance: T-SIM-PLAN passes over 100 seeded years.
rationale: The baseline has to be the rota itself, untouched.

text: Simulated sick calls per year shall average within 10% of the configured rate times the scheduled shifts.
acceptance: T-SIM-SICK passes over 10000 seeded years; the expected count is computed in the test from the configured rate, not copied from a run.
rationale: Every comparison scales with how often the phone rings.

text: The model shall reproduce the unchecked habit (most reliable first, days not counted) and shall count the run-cap breaches it causes.
acceptance: T-SIM-HABIT passes: an independent checker reading the final duty grid finds exactly as many runs over the cap as the model reported, over 1000 seeded years, and the number is above zero.
rationale: The baseline being replaced must be modelled honestly, including what it costs the person who always says yes.

text: Two runs with the same seed and parameters shall produce byte-identical event traces.
acceptance: T-SIM-DET passes.
rationale: A comparison nobody can reproduce settles nothing.

text: The controller shall turn sick calls into ordered proposals, and only a person shall turn a proposal into an assignment.
acceptance: All children verified.
rationale: The program holds the rule; the coordinator holds the decision.

text: The controller shall never list a candidate whose assignment would break the run cap, a role rule, or any other check in the rota's checkRota.
acceptance: T-CTL-LAW passes: 10000 seeded sick calls, every listed candidate judged lawful by checkRota run independently of the controller.
rationale: The habit broke the cap about 5 times a year in the sizing run; the controller exists partly to make that impossible.

text: The controller shall list candidates in exactly the order the adopted clause defines, with ties broken by a seeded lottery whose draw is logged.
acceptance: T-CTL-ORDER passes against a reference ordering written from the clause alone, over 10000 seeded calls.
rationale: An order that drifts from the clause is a new rule nobody adopted.

text: The controller shall record an assignment only on an injected accept signal naming the person, and shall record every decline.
acceptance: T-CTL-HUMAN passes: with no accept injected the duty grid is unchanged after the shift starts, and every injected decline appears in the log.
rationale: Who decides stays a person; the record shows who was asked, not only who said yes.

text: When no lawful candidate remains, the controller shall report the shift as uncovered and name the rule that excluded each remaining person.
acceptance: T-CTL-EMPTY passes on fixtures where each rule alone is the binding one.
rationale: An empty slot with a named cause is a staffing question for the clinic; an unlawful cover hides it.

text: The controller shall make the same proposals under run() and under runRealtime() with a fake clock and the same injected signals.
acceptance: T-CTL-SAME passes: scripted mornings, proposal logs compared entry by entry.
rationale: The rule tested in simulation must be the rule that runs.

text: Every call, proposal, lottery draw, accept and decline shall go to an append-only log, and replaying the log shall reproduce every proposal.
acceptance: T-CTL-LOG passes over 1000 seeded live-style runs.
rationale: Anyone who thinks they are asked too often can check, without trusting the coordinator or the program.

text: The draft rule's effect shall be measured against the habit before the clinic is asked to adopt it.
acceptance: All children verified.
rationale: The clinic should see what it is choosing between, in shifts.

text: Under the draft rule, the gap between the most and least covers per role per year shall average at most 3.5 shifts.
acceptance: A-PWR-SPREAD over 1000 seeded years writes TPM-SPREAD; the sizing run gave 2.8 for the draft rule and 4.7 for the lawful habit.
rationale: The habit concentrates cover on whoever says yes most often.

text: The draft rule shall leave no more than 1.5 percentage points more shifts uncovered than the lawful habit.
acceptance: A-PWR-COST over 1000 seeded years writes TPM-UNCOVERED-COST; the sizing run gave -1.0 points.
rationale: Fairness that empties shifts would be a bad trade; the sizing run says it does not.

text: The analysis shall report the price of the run cap: the extra share of shifts left uncovered when the habit is made lawful, with a 95% interval.
acceptance: A-PWR-PRICE reports the difference and its interval over 1000 seeded years, and states the assumed acceptance and sickness rates beside it.
rationale: The habit filled about 8 points more shifts by spending the rest of the most reliable person. That trade belongs to the clinic, not the coordinator.

text: Cover shall be fitted to the clinic's real team and adopted by the clinic before it runs.
acceptance: All children verified.
rationale: The lab can build the scaffold; only the clinic can make it a rule.

text: The sickness rate and each role's acceptance rates shall be taken from the clinic's own records of past sick calls, replacing the assumed values.
acceptance: I-REAL-RATES: the rates file cites its source records and the CV-PWR analyses are re-run on it.
rationale: The sizing numbers rest on invented acceptance rates (0.9 down to 0.3).

text: Cover shall read the clinic's real rota and judge lawfulness with the rota project's own checkRota.
acceptance: I-REAL-ROTA: the import of checkRota is from the rota tree, and the CV-CTL-LAW test runs against it.
rationale: Two different readings of the policy would be two policies. The rota tree is not in this lab today.

text: The clinic shall adopt, amend or reject the call-in clause in writing, through whoever owns POLICY.md.
acceptance: I-REAL-ADOPT: a signed copy of the clause, or a written rejection, is filed.
rationale: Who decides the order of asking is the whole question; it cannot be the lab.

text: The coordinator shall run Cover for one full rota period, and every sick call in that period shall appear in its log.
acceptance: D-REAL-TRIAL: the period's log matches the clinic's own list of sick calls one for one.
rationale: A rule nobody runs on a real morning is still a draft.
